⛰️ Suikerbosrand — Saturday 14 November
📍 Suikerbosrand Nature Reserve, near Heidelberg
📅 Saturday 14 November 2026
⏰ Start 07:00
🥾 Bokmakierie Trail — 10 km loop
💰 R45 per adult entrance (vehicle fees additional)
Difficulty: challenging — moderate to hard, with repeated climbs and descents, rocky terrain and rugged sections.
🌄 What to expect
Sweeping Highveld views · rocky ridges and boulder sections · grasslands, sugarbush and protea · a stunning sunrise if we’re lucky!
🎒 What to bring
At least 2–3 L of water · snacks or a packed lunch · sun protection (hat, sunscreen, sunglasses) · sturdy hiking shoes with good grip · hiking poles if you use them.
There are no water points on the trail.

DFS Health & Fitness Tips 💪

Your DFS tip library — tap any card to open it 👇

A gentle 12-minute full-body flow that’s lovely on a rest day, before class, or any morning your body feels stiff. Bouncing, shaking, twisting and tapping to get things moving and release tension — no equipment, just you.

The format: 16 moves, 45 seconds each, low impact throughout. Heel drops, body bounces, chest openers, pliés, hip switches, knee slaps, booty kickers and a full body shake out to finish.

Perfect for mornings, movement breaks or travel days. Follow along with the video — every move is cued out loud.

▶️ Watch the 12-minute flow

Squats are a powerhouse move in our routines: they build lower-body strength, tighten your core and power up your jumps and turns on the dance floor. To get the most out of every drop — and keep your body safe — keep these in mind:

  • Chest up, back straight — keep your posture tall and proud to protect your spine.
  • Core engaged — brace as you lower down so you stay balanced and stable through the rhythm.
  • Knees behind toes, weight in heels — push your hips back as if sitting in a chair, with your weight planted firmly in your heels.

Master your form, bring the energy, and let’s crush those dance fitness goals together! 💪

Ever wonder why we keep working lunges into the routine? They’re an absolute powerhouse for dance and overall strength. Here’s why they’re so good for you:

  • Lower body strength — they target your quads, hamstrings and glutes, giving you the power and drive for those high-energy dance moves.
  • Core stability — keeping your back straight and core engaged protects your lower back and improves your posture.
  • Mobility & coordination — each leg works independently, which irons out muscle imbalances and keeps your joints happy.

Form check: front knee at 90 degrees, back knee hovering just above the floor, and keep that back straight! Let’s keep crushing it on the dance floor. 👑

Four everyday foods that help your body settle and recover after class:

  • Fatty fish (salmon, sardines) — rich in Omega-3s that reduce inflammation. Great for joints after Zumba.
  • Berries (blueberries, raspberries) — antioxidants that lower inflammatory markers. A perfect post-class snack.
  • Extra virgin olive oil — contains oleocanthal, which has anti-inflammatory effects. Use it for dressings or roasted veg.
  • Turmeric — its curcumin is a powerful anti-inflammatory. Try it in curries or golden milk, and pair it with black pepper so your body absorbs it.

Stay strong, recover well, and keep dancing! — your DFS team 💕

A quick breakfast you can build the night before and grab on the way out:

  • Creamy Greek yogurt — high protein.
  • Cubed papaya — vitamin C and digestive enzymes.
  • Nuts & seeds mix (2 walnuts, 1 brazil nut, pepitas, cranberries) — selenium, Omega-3s and antioxidants.

DFS girls: fuelled and fierce. 👑

Deshni’s own pickled beet recipe for the Zumba girls:

  • Boil whole adult beets with the skin on for about an hour.
  • Cool & slip — once cooled, the skin slips off with a light rub.
  • Add spices — 2 whole star anise and a few cloves.
  • Add vinegar and jar it up.

Why it’s worth it: nitrates for stamina and endurance, fibre for digestion, antioxidants to fight inflammation and help muscles recover, plus potassium, magnesium, iron and manganese.

How much: a small portion with meals — 2 to 3 slices, about half a cup — is perfect. Don’t overdo it with added sugar and salt.

Not all cinnamon is the same. Ceylon is the healthier choice for daily use — its coumarin levels are very low, so it’s fine long term. Cassia (the common supermarket one) is much higher in coumarin, which can strain the liver if you take a lot of it every day.

Ways to use Ceylon: infuse a piece of bark in hot water or overnight in a water bottle; sprinkle the powder over oats, yogurt or fruit; add a dash to coffee, lattes or protein shakes. Supplements are optional — check with a doctor first.

  • Ceylon: start with ½ to 1 teaspoon daily, safely up to about 3 g.
  • Cassia: keep to no more than ¼ teaspoon a day, and occasionally rather than daily.

Beyond the kitchen: it may help insulin sensitivity and blood sugar balance (which matters for hormonal health such as PCOS), support the stress response, and ease menstrual discomfort.

For information purposes only. Always speak to your doctor before making dietary changes — this is not a substitute for medical advice.

✨ Meet Deshni

Get to know her below 👇

1How do you balance your energy from a corporate environment to the dance floor?▾

Honestly, Zumba is how I reset. My corporate world is structured, strategic, and high-pressure — the dance floor is where I switch off the noise and just move. It’s less about balancing and more about transforming my energy from focused to free.

2What’s more intimidating — Monday boardroom or introducing a new Zumba routine?▾

Surprisingly… introducing a new routine! In the boardroom I know my content. On the dance floor, I need to win people over in seconds — if they’re not feeling the vibe, you know immediately 😄

3🔥 What’s your secret to keeping your boss energy AND dance floor charisma?▾

Authenticity. Whether I’m in a boardroom or on the dance floor, I show up as myself. The difference is the delivery — one is more structured, the other is more expressive — but the confidence comes from the same place.

4😅 Who sweats more — your staff or your Zumba students?▾

Definitely the Zumba students! My team sweats under deadlines… my Zumba divas sweat because I push them 😄

5💡 How do you turn stress into motivation?▾

I move. Whether it’s dancing, training, or just getting out of the mental space — movement clears my mind and resets my focus. By the time I’m done, stress turns into clarity.

6🏡 What does your family think about your Zumba moves?▾

They’ve accepted that I will randomly start dancing anywhere — kitchen, lounge, wherever 😄 They’re my biggest supporters… even if they laugh at me sometimes!

7👀 What’s the one thing people learn quickly about you?▾

That I bring energy into every room — whether it’s a client meeting or a Zumba class. I don’t do anything halfway.

8💛 Why Zumba? If not Zumba, what else would you teach?▾

Zumba is powerful because it doesn’t feel like exercise — it feels like joy. That’s what I love. If not Zumba, I’d probably do something else that blends movement and energy — maybe strength training or even something like dance fitness bootcamps.

1How do you balance your energy from a corporate environment to the dance floor?▾

Corporate has taught me discipline, Zumba taught me to release. Coffee fuels the corporate me throughout the day, music releases the real me.

2What’s more intimidating — your Monday morning boardroom presentation or introducing a new routine/song to your Zumba class?▾

Boardroom, 100%. The boardroom doesn’t dance back if you mess up. My Zumba class will hype me up even if I forget the steps 😄 And if I’m nervous, I make it a move and call it a choreo.

3What’s your secret to keeping your boss energy to dance floor charisma?▾

Desh has drilled this into me for 11 years and continues to challenge me LOL. I am learning that confidence is a cue, not a feeling. At work I lead teams, on the floor I lead movement — and I have learned it is the same skill, and that it makes people feel safe enough to go all in.

4Who sweats more around you — your staff at work or new Zumba students?▾

Zumba students, no contest. I’m nicer with my work teams than I am with the divas on the dance floor 😂

5How do you turn stress into motivation?▾

I move, literally. Yoga, dance, anything. Stress sits in your hips and can cripple you, so I reframe it — it just means my body cares about this. Then I channel whatever it is into movement. Trust me, I always feel better after movement.

6What does your family think about your Zumba moves?▾

They roast me at home and hype me up outside 😂 They think I’m showing off and I tell them it’s research. Haha! But secretly they’ve all tried some of my moves at family events — overall very supportive.

7What’s the one thing that people learn quickly about you?▾

That I show up with intention. Whether I’m running a project or running a class, people feel seen. And that I notice people — if someone’s ‘absent’ in class or at work, it matters to me.

8Why Zumba? If you didn’t teach Zumba, what else would you teach?▾

Zumba because after 11 years on the floor, I know what it feels like to find yourself in movement. I want to give people that for 60 mins, 2x a week. Joy is medicine. If not Zumba, probably yoga + kindness — I’m terrible at sitting still anyway; we’d probably be rolling down on our tummies if nothing else!

“By day I drive growth. By night I drive beats. Either way — I bring the energy.”

What does your family think about your Zumba moves?
